The seams are bilinear filtering
  blending across atlas slot
  boundaries: at a face's UV edge the
  GPU averages its texel with the
  neighbor's texel (gutter or the next
  face's slot), drawing a thin
  off-color line. Nearest sampling 
  samples exactly one texel — no 
  averaging — so a face's edge can only
  ever be its own paint. No blend = no
  seam, no bleed, no red-on-black. And
  since paint is flat colors, nearest
  loses nothing visually (you don't
  want smoothing on flat fills anyway).
  That's why this is the real fix and
  the padding/bleed tuning never could
  be — those fight the symptom, nearest
  removes the mechanism.

  Two honest caveats, so I don't
  over-promise again:
  1. It's global. It flips the Scene3D
  texture sampler for every mesh, so
  the whole game's textures become
  crisp/blocky instead of smooth. Given
  the PSX-style look that's probably
  fine (the code even anticipates
  this), but it's a visible change —
  your call.
  2. Mipmaps. If the sampler does
  mipmapped minification, faces seen at
  a distance could still average
  neighbor texels. If so I'll disable
  mips for this texture too — same fix,
  one extra line.
